sapience_notes.subject: setup-sapience-mcp.sh token resolution
sapience_notes.value: The writer's resolve_token() (deleted in this task) read ~/.sapience/config.json's `.token` field, distinct from `.host` which resolve_host() still reads; a prior version of this plan's negative-control fixture must set config.json's token under the key `token`, not `SAPIENCE_TOKEN`.

sapience_notes.subject: verify-sapience-mcp.sh fail() output under --quiet
sapience_notes.value: fail() prints only the bare word FAIL when --quiet is set, not the named [FAIL] (b) ... remedy message; a test asserting on the remedy text must invoke the verifier without --quiet.

sapience_notes.subject: setup-sapience-mcp.sh process_write whole-entry comparison
sapience_notes.value: process_write() compares the existing entry to the canonical one with jq's $a == $b over the whole JSON object, so ANY divergence (including an extra env key like SAPIENCE_TOKEN not present in the canonical shape) triggers a full wholesale replacement, not a per-field patch -- this is what makes a token-bearing legacy entry self-heal on the next writer run with no special-casing needed.

sapience_notes.subject: verify-touched.sh scope in a multi-task shared working tree
sapience_notes.value: verify-touched.sh derives its touched-path corpus from the full working-tree diff, not from a single task's own declared file_scope -- so in a repo where multiple /orchestrate dispatches run concurrently against the same working tree, an unrelated sibling task's uncommitted changes can pull in and fail an unrelated suite (observed: task 677's in-flight orchestration work caused test-stall-reprompt-wiring.sh to be selected and fail during a task-682 dispatch whose own git status --short showed only one unrelated file modified).

sapience_notes.subject: test-sapience-mcp-registration.sh header-comment Phase labels
sapience_notes.value: The suite's existing header-comment sections labeled 'Phase 2/3/4/5' refer to an ancestor task's own plan structure (Writer/Hook/Installer/Verifier cases), not to the current token-removal task's Phase 1-5 structure -- a future case addition for a different task should avoid reusing the word 'Phase N' in a new header section to prevent two different meanings colliding in the same file.
